# Azure Managed Grafana

AVM Resource Module for Azure Managed Grafana (`Microsoft.Dashboard/grafana`).

It deploys a Standard tier workspace with AzAPI and supports:

- instance size, Grafana major version, zone redundancy, deterministic outbound IPs, public network access, API keys / service accounts, plugins and Grafana server settings (SMTP, snapshots, user permissions, CSRF, alert screenshots);
- linking Azure Monitor workspaces (managed Prometheus) to the workspace;
- managed private endpoints from Grafana to data sources (`managed_private_endpoints`, implemented by the `modules/managed-private-endpoint` submodule);
- the standard AVM interfaces: role assignments, lock, diagnostic settings, managed identities, private endpoints and tags.

The module only manages the Grafana workspace and resources scoped to it. It never creates anything in the scope of another service.

## Data source access

Grafana's identity needs roles on the services it reads, for example `Monitoring Data Reader` on Azure Monitor workspaces (managed Prometheus) and `Monitoring Reader` on the resources or resource groups whose metrics and logs it visualises. Linking an Azure Monitor workspace with `azure_monitor_workspace_integrations` does not grant that access.

Those roles are granted by the modules that own the data sources, through their own `role_assignments` input, using this module's `system_assigned_mi_principal_id` output:

```hcl
module "postgresql" {
  source  = "Azure/avm-res-dbforpostgresql-flexibleserver/azurerm"
  version = "<pinned version>"
  # ...
  role_assignments = {
    grafana = {
      role_definition_id_or_name = "Monitoring Reader"
      principal_id               = module.grafana.system_assigned_mi_principal_id
      principal_type             = "ServicePrincipal"
    }
  }
}
```

When private DNS zones are managed centrally (for example by Azure Policy), set `private_endpoints_manage_dns_zone_group = false` so the module does not create private DNS zone groups for its private endpoints.

## Production choices

These inputs are left to each deployment because the right value depends on the environment:

- **Network access.** `public_network_access_enabled` defaults to `null`: public access is disabled as soon as `private_endpoints` is not empty, and enabled otherwise so that a workspace without private endpoints stays reachable. Set it explicitly to choose, and match the built-in Azure Policy "Azure Managed Grafana workspaces should disable public network access" if it is assigned.
- **Zone redundancy.** Recommended for production where available, but it is offered in a few regions only, costs extra and can only be chosen at creation. `zone_redundancy_enabled` therefore defaults to `false`, so that the module deploys in every region; this deviates from AVM spec SFR5 on purpose. Decide before the first apply: changing it later replaces the workspace and everything stored in it.
- **Lock.** Use `lock = { kind = "CanNotDelete" }` in production. A `ReadOnly` lock also blocks updates and the managed private endpoint refresh.
- **External snapshots** are disabled by default (`grafana_configurations.snapshots_external_enabled = false`), as the security guidance recommends; the service default is enabled.
- **Grafana version.** Major upgrades can't be undone, and Microsoft upgrades workspaces itself when a version retires. After that, raise `grafana_major_version` to match the `grafana_version` output, or add `properties.grafanaMajorVersion` to `ignore_body_changes.dashboard_grafana`. `security_csrf_always_check` and `users_editors_can_admin` only exist up to Grafana 11; the module rejects them for Grafana 12 and later.

## Backup and disaster recovery

Azure Managed Grafana has no backup, restore or cross-region failover of dashboards, folders, alert rules or data sources. Keep them as code (for example with the `grafana/grafana` Terraform provider) so that they can be redeployed, and for a regional outage deploy a second workspace in another region. A `CanNotDelete` lock protects the workspace against accidental deletion.

## Usage notes

- **Identity.** No identity is configured by default. Set `managed_identities = { system_assigned = true }` (or a single user-assigned identity) so Grafana can query Azure data sources. The service accepts exactly one identity.
- **Access to Grafana** is controlled with Azure RBAC through `role_assignments`, using the built-in `Grafana Admin`, `Grafana Editor`, `Grafana Viewer` and `Grafana Limited Viewer` roles. Automation (for example the `grafana/grafana` Terraform provider) can authenticate with a Microsoft Entra token for the audience `https://dashboard.azure.com`, so `api_key_enabled` can stay `false`.
- **Diagnostic settings.** Azure Managed Grafana exports three log categories (`GrafanaLoginEvents`, `GrafanaUsageInsightsEvents`, `GrafanaAlertAuthFailure`; category groups `allLogs` and `audit`) and `AllMetrics`. Azure returns the categories that are not selected as disabled entries, so the module sends them too, which keeps plans clean. That catalog is fixed in `locals.tf`: if Azure adds a category, plans show a diff until the module lists it. `log_analytics_destination_type` is accepted by the standard interface but is not sent, because the service does not support it. A setting without `name` is named `diag-<workspace name>`.
- **Private endpoints.** Unless set, names default per map key: `pep-<workspace>-<key>` for the endpoint, `nic-<endpoint name>` for its network interface and `pse-<workspace>-<key>` for the connection. Endpoints inherit `tags` and the workspace `lock` unless they set their own; `lock = { kind = "None" }` leaves an endpoint unlocked.
- **Role assignments** are replaced when their principal or role changes, because Azure does not allow updating an existing assignment.
- **Create-only settings.** Changing `zone_redundancy_enabled` replaces the workspace and everything stored in it; zone redundancy is only available in some regions (see *Reliability in Azure Managed Grafana* on Microsoft Learn). Every property of a managed private endpoint is create-only too. `sku_size` can be increased from `X1` to `X2` but not decreased.
- **Plugins.** `grafana_plugins` is applied as additions: removing a plugin from the set may not uninstall it.
- **Managed private endpoints** remain `Pending` until the connection is approved on the target resource, by whoever owns it. Grafana only uses an approved endpoint after the workspace is refreshed: the module refreshes it when endpoints are added or removed, and again whenever `managed_private_endpoints_refresh_trigger` changes, so change it after each approval. The `managed-private-endpoint` submodule has no role assignment or lock inputs: role assignments on a managed private endpoint grant nothing useful, and it inherits the workspace lock.
- **SMTP.** Azure does not support enabling SMTP while the workspace is being created: add `grafana_configurations.smtp` in a later apply. The password (`smtp_password`) is ephemeral and write-only, so it is never stored in plan or state. Azure rejects any update of the workspace whose SMTP settings lack the password, so the module sends it with every update: supply it on every apply, for example from Key Vault. After rotating it, change `smtp_password_version` to push the new value without any other change.
- **SKU.** Only `Standard` can be deployed; the `Essential` tier is deprecated and retires on 31 March 2027.
- **Terraform 1.11** or later is required, because of the ephemeral, write-only SMTP password.

## Required Inputs

The following input variables are required:

### <a name="input_location"></a> [location](#input\_location)

Description: Azure region where the Grafana workspace and its telemetry deployment are created.

Type: `string`

### <a name="input_name"></a> [name](#input\_name)

Description: The name of the Azure Managed Grafana workspace. It is also used as the host name prefix of the workspace endpoint.

Type: `string`

### <a name="input_parent_id"></a> [parent\_id](#input\_parent\_id)

Description: The fully-qualified ARM resource ID of the existing resource group into which the Grafana workspace will be deployed.

Type: `string`

## Optional Inputs

The following input variables are optional (have default values):

### <a name="input_api_key_enabled"></a> [api\_key\_enabled](#input\_api\_key\_enabled)

Description: Enables API keys and Grafana service accounts. Defaults to `false`.

Leave this disabled when automation authenticates with Microsoft Entra ID tokens (audience `https://dashboard.azure.com`),  
which is the recommended approach: service account tokens bypass Entra ID and are long-lived secrets.

Type: `bool`

Default: `false`

### <a name="input_azure_monitor_workspace_integrations"></a> [azure\_monitor\_workspace\_integrations](#input\_azure\_monitor\_workspace\_integrations)

Description: A map of Azure Monitor workspaces (managed Prometheus) to link to Grafana. Each link provisions a Prometheus data source in Grafana.  
The map key is deliberately arbitrary to avoid issues where map keys may be unknown at plan time.

Linking does not grant access: Grafana's identity also needs `Monitoring Data Reader` on each workspace, granted by the module that manages the workspace (see the `system_assigned_mi_principal_id` output).

- `resource_id` - The resource ID of the Azure Monitor workspace.

Type:

```hcl
map(object({
    resource_id = string
  }))
```

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_deterministic_outbound_ip_enabled"></a> [deterministic\_outbound\_ip\_enabled](#input\_deterministic\_outbound\_ip\_enabled)

Description: Use deterministic outbound IPs, so that data sources behind a firewall can allow-list Grafana. The IPs are exported in the `outbound_ips` output. Defaults to `false`.

Type: `bool`

Default: `false`

### <a name="input_diagnostic_settings"></a> [diagnostic\_settings](#input\_diagnostic\_settings)

Description: A map of diagnostic settings to create on the resource. The map key is deliberately arbitrary to avoid issues where map keys maybe unknown at plan time.

- `name` - (Optional) The name of the diagnostic setting. One will be generated if not set, however this will not be unique if you want to create multiple diagnostic setting resources.
- `logs` - (Optional) A set of log entries to send to the destination. Each entry has the following attributes:
  - `category` - (Optional) The name of a specific log category to enable. Mutually exclusive with `category_group`.
  - `category_group` - (Optional) The name of a log category group to enable (for example, `allLogs` or `audit`). Mutually exclusive with `category`.
  - `enabled` - (Optional) Whether the log entry is enabled. Defaults to `true`.
  - `retention_policy` - (Optional) The retention policy for the log entry.
    - `days` - (Optional) The retention period in days. Defaults to `0` (retain indefinitely).
    - `enabled` - (Optional) Whether the retention policy is enabled. Defaults to `false`.
- `metrics` - (Optional) A set of metric entries to send to the destination. Each entry has the following attributes:
  - `category` - (Optional) The name of the metric category to enable.
  - `enabled` - (Optional) Whether the metric entry is enabled. Defaults to `true`.
  - `retention_policy` - (Optional) The retention policy for the metric entry, with the same `days` and `enabled` attributes as `logs.retention_policy`.
- `log_analytics_destination_type` - (Optional) The destination type for the diagnostic setting. Possible values are `Dedicated` and `AzureDiagnostics`. Defaults to `Dedicated`.
- `workspace_resource_id` - (Optional) The resource ID of the log analytics workspace to send logs and metrics to.
- `storage_account_resource_id` - (Optional) The resource ID of the storage account to send logs and metrics to.
- `event_hub_authorization_rule_resource_id` - (Optional) The resource ID of the event hub authorization rule to send logs and metrics to.
- `event_hub_name` - (Optional) The name of the event hub. If none is specified, the default event hub will be selected.
- `marketplace_partner_resource_id` - (Optional) The full ARM resource ID of the Marketplace resource to which you would like to send Diagnostic Logs.

Type:

```hcl
map(object({
    name = optional(string, null)
    logs = optional(set(object({
      category       = optional(string, null)
      category_group = optional(string, null)
      enabled        = optional(bool, true)
      retention_policy = optional(object({
        days    = optional(number, 0)
        enabled = optional(bool, false)
      }), {})
    })), [])
    metrics = optional(set(object({
      category = optional(string, null)
      enabled  = optional(bool, true)
      retention_policy = optional(object({
        days    = optional(number, 0)
        enabled = optional(bool, false)
      }), {})
    })), [])
    log_analytics_destination_type           = optional(string, "Dedicated")
    workspace_resource_id                    = optional(string, null)
    storage_account_resource_id              = optional(string, null)
    event_hub_authorization_rule_resource_id = optional(string, null)
    event_hub_name                           = optional(string, null)
    marketplace_partner_resource_id          = optional(string, null)
  }))
```

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_enable_telemetry"></a> [enable\_telemetry](#input\_enable\_telemetry)

Description: This variable controls whether or not telemetry is enabled for the module.  
For more information see <https://aka.ms/avm/telemetryinfo>.  
If it is set to false, then no telemetry will be collected.

Type: `bool`

Default: `true`

### <a name="input_grafana_configurations"></a> [grafana\_configurations](#input\_grafana\_configurations)

Description: Grafana server settings. Unset (`null`) values are not sent: a new workspace gets the service default and an existing one  
keeps its current value.

- `smtp` - (Optional) SMTP settings used for alert notifications and reports. The password is set with `smtp_password`.
  - `enabled` - (Optional) Defaults to `true`.
  - `host` - SMTP server host and port, e.g. `smtp.office365.com:587`.
  - `from_address` - Address used as sender.
  - `from_name` - (Optional) Display name used as sender.
  - `user` - (Optional) SMTP user name.
  - `start_tls_policy` - (Optional) One of `OpportunisticStartTLS`, `MandatoryStartTLS`, `NoStartTLS`. Defaults to `MandatoryStartTLS`.
  - `skip_verify` - (Optional) Skip TLS certificate verification. Defaults to `false`.
- `security_csrf_always_check` - (Optional) Always run the CSRF check, even for requests without a session cookie. Grafana 11 and earlier only.
- `snapshots_external_enabled` - (Optional) Allow publishing snapshots to an external snapshot server. Defaults to `false`, as the Azure Managed Grafana security guidance recommends; the service default is `true`.
- `unified_alerting_screenshots_capture_enabled` - (Optional) Attach panel screenshots to alert notifications.
- `users_editors_can_admin` - (Optional) Let Editors administer the dashboards, folders and teams they create. Grafana 11 and earlier only.
- `users_viewers_can_edit` - (Optional) Let Viewers use Explore and edit (but not save) dashboards.

Type:

```hcl
object({
    smtp = optional(object({
      enabled          = optional(bool, true)
      host             = string
      from_address     = string
      from_name        = optional(string, null)
      user             = optional(string, null)
      start_tls_policy = optional(string, "MandatoryStartTLS")
      skip_verify      = optional(bool, false)
    }), null)
    security_csrf_always_check                   = optional(bool, null)
    snapshots_external_enabled                   = optional(bool, false)
    unified_alerting_screenshots_capture_enabled = optional(bool, null)
    users_editors_can_admin                      = optional(bool, null)
    users_viewers_can_edit                       = optional(bool, null)
  })
```

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_grafana_major_version"></a> [grafana\_major\_version](#input\_grafana\_major\_version)

Description: The major Grafana version to run. Defaults to `12`.

Microsoft applies minor and patch updates automatically. Major upgrades are opt-in until a version retires; Microsoft then  
upgrades the remaining workspaces itself. Upgrades can't be undone: after Microsoft upgraded a workspace, raise this input  
to match (the `grafana_version` output shows the running version), or add `properties.grafanaMajorVersion` to
`ignore_body_changes.dashboard_grafana` to let Microsoft manage the version. From Grafana 13, Azure-authenticated  
Prometheus uses the `grafana-azureprometheus-datasource` plugin.

Type: `string`

Default: `"12"`

### <a name="input_grafana_plugins"></a> [grafana\_plugins](#input\_grafana\_plugins)

Description: A set of additional plugin IDs to install, e.g. `grafana-clock-panel`. An empty set (the default) leaves plugins unmanaged, and the property is not sent.

The service applies this list as additions, so removing a plugin from the set may not uninstall it from the workspace.

Type: `set(string)`

Default: `[]`

### <a name="input_ignore_body_changes"></a> [ignore\_body\_changes](#input\_ignore\_body\_changes)

Description: Paths in each resource's `body` whose changes the AzAPI provider ignores. Prefer Terraform's `lifecycle.ignore_changes` when the paths are static; use this variable when the paths must be derived from variables or other non-static values.

Paths use dot notation, for example `properties.grafanaPlugins`. Individual list items cannot be targeted — ignore the whole list property instead. Configuration changes at an ignored path are **not** sent to Azure until that path is removed from the list.

Supplying a non-empty value requires Terraform 1.11 or later, because `ignore_body_changes` is a write-only argument. Changes take effect only after an apply, because the value is held in provider-private state.

- `authorization_locks` - Ignored body paths for the management locks on the workspace and its private endpoints.
- `authorization_role_assignments` - Ignored body paths for role assignments on the workspace, on its private endpoints, and for its managed identity.
- `dashboard_grafana` - Ignored body paths for the Grafana workspace managed by this module.
- `insights_diagnostic_settings` - Ignored body paths for the diagnostic settings.
- `network_private_endpoints` - Ignored body paths for the private endpoints.
- `network_private_endpoints_private_dns_zone_groups` - Ignored body paths for the private DNS zone groups.
- `dashboard_grafana_managed_private_endpoints` - Override slot for the `managed-private-endpoint` submodule. Supply only the keys you want to override.
  - `dashboard_grafana_managed_private_endpoints` - Ignored body paths for the managed private endpoint managed by the submodule.

Type:

```hcl
object({
    authorization_locks                               = optional(list(string), [])
    authorization_role_assignments                    = optional(list(string), [])
    dashboard_grafana                                 = optional(list(string), [])
    insights_diagnostic_settings                      = optional(list(string), [])
    network_private_endpoints                         = optional(list(string), [])
    network_private_endpoints_private_dns_zone_groups = optional(list(string), [])

    dashboard_grafana_managed_private_endpoints = optional(object({
      dashboard_grafana_managed_private_endpoints = optional(list(string), [])
    }), {})
  })
```

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_lock"></a> [lock](#input\_lock)

Description: Controls the Resource Lock configuration for this resource. The following properties can be specified:

- `kind` - (Required) The type of lock. Possible values are `\"CanNotDelete\"` and `\"ReadOnly\"`.
- `name` - (Optional) The name of the lock. If not specified, it defaults to `lock-<workspace name>`. Changing this forces the creation of a new resource.
- `notes` - (Optional) Notes about the lock. This value maps to `Microsoft.Authorization/locks.properties.notes`.

The default, `null`, creates no lock. The lock also applies to every private endpoint created by this module unless that endpoint sets its own `lock` (use `kind = "None"` to leave an endpoint unlocked).  
Prefer `CanNotDelete` in production: a `ReadOnly` lock also blocks later updates of the workspace and the refresh of managed private endpoints.

Type:

```hcl
object({
    kind  = string
    name  = optional(string, null)
    notes = optional(string, null)
  })
```

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_managed_identities"></a> [managed\_identities](#input\_managed\_identities)

Description: Controls the Managed Identity configuration on this resource. The following properties can be specified:

- `system_assigned` - (Optional) Specifies if the System Assigned Managed Identity should be enabled.
- `user_assigned_resource_ids` - (Optional) Specifies a list of User Assigned Managed Identity resource IDs to be assigned to this resource.

Type:

```hcl
object({
    system_assigned            = optional(bool, false)
    user_assigned_resource_ids = optional(set(string), [])
  })
```

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_managed_private_endpoints"></a> [managed\_private\_endpoints](#input\_managed\_private\_endpoints)

Description: A map of managed private endpoints that Grafana uses to reach data sources over Private Link.  
The map key is deliberately arbitrary to avoid issues where map keys may be unknown at plan time. All attributes can only be set at creation; changing them replaces the managed private endpoint.

Each connection must then be approved on the target resource, by whoever owns it, and the workspace refreshed: Grafana  
only uses an approved endpoint after a refresh. The module refreshes whenever endpoints are added or removed; after an  
approval, change `managed_private_endpoints_refresh_trigger` to refresh again.

- `name` - The name of the managed private endpoint.
- `private_link_resource_id` - The resource ID of the target resource, e.g. an Azure Monitor workspace or an Azure Data Explorer cluster.
- `group_ids` - The private link sub-resources to connect to, e.g. `["prometheusMetrics"]` for an Azure Monitor workspace.
- `private_link_resource_region` - (Optional) The region of the target resource.
- `private_link_service_url` - (Optional) The URL of the data store behind the Private Link service, as used in the Grafana data source, without protocol and port.
- `request_message` - (Optional) A message shown to the approver of the connection request.

`private_link_resource_id` is not validated because it accepts many resource types.

Type:

```hcl
map(object({
    name                         = string
    private_link_resource_id     = string
    group_ids                    = list(string)
    private_link_resource_region = optional(string, null)
    private_link_service_url     = optional(string, null)
    request_message              = optional(string, null)
  }))
```

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_managed_private_endpoints_refresh_trigger"></a> [managed\_private\_endpoints\_refresh\_trigger](#input\_managed\_private\_endpoints\_refresh\_trigger)

Description: Change this value, e.g. to a date, to refresh the managed private endpoints again, typically after their connections were approved on the target resources. Ignored when `managed_private_endpoints` is empty.

Type: `string`

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_private_endpoints"></a> [private\_endpoints](#input\_private\_endpoints)

Description: A map of private endpoints to create on the Grafana workspace. The map key is deliberately arbitrary to avoid issues where map keys maybe unknown at plan time.

- `name` - (Optional) The name of the private endpoint. One will be generated if not set.
- `role_assignments` - (Optional) A map of role assignments to create on the private endpoint. The map key is deliberately arbitrary to avoid issues where map keys maybe unknown at plan time. See `var.role_assignments` for more information.
  - `name` - (Optional) The name of the role assignment. If not set, a random UUID will be generated. Changing this forces the creation of a new resource.
  - `role_definition_id_or_name` - The ID or name of the role definition to assign to the principal.
  - `principal_id` - The ID of the principal to assign the role to.
  - `description` - (Optional) The description of the role assignment.
  - `skip_service_principal_aad_check` - (Optional) If set to true, skips the Azure Active Directory check for the service principal in the tenant. Defaults to false.
  - `condition` - (Optional) The condition which will be used to scope the role assignment.
  - `condition_version` - (Optional) The version of the condition syntax. Leave as `null` if you are not using a condition, if you are then valid values are '2.0'.
  - `delegated_managed_identity_resource_id` - (Optional) The delegated Azure Resource Id which contains a Managed Identity. Changing this forces a new resource to be created. This field is only used in cross-tenant scenario.
  - `principal_type` - (Optional) The type of the `principal_id`. Possible values are `User`, `Group` and `ServicePrincipal`. It is necessary to explicitly set this attribute when creating role assignments if the principal creating the assignment is constrained by ABAC rules that filters on the PrincipalType attribute.
- `lock` - (Optional) The lock level to apply to the private endpoint. Default is `None`. Possible values are `None`, `CanNotDelete`, and `ReadOnly`.
  - `kind` - (Required) The type of lock. Possible values are `\"CanNotDelete\"` and `\"ReadOnly\"`.
  - `name` - (Optional) The name of the lock. If not specified, a name will be generated based on the `kind` value. Changing this forces the creation of a new resource.
  - `notes` - (Optional) Notes about the lock. This value maps to `Microsoft.Authorization/locks.properties.notes`.
- `tags` - (Optional) A mapping of tags to assign to the private endpoint.
- `subnet_resource_id` - The resource ID of the subnet to deploy the private endpoint in.
- `subresource_name` (Optional) - The name of the sub resource for the private endpoint.
- `private_dns_zone_group_name` - (Optional) The name of the private DNS zone group. One will be generated if not set.
- `private_dns_zone_resource_ids` - (Optional) A set of resource IDs of private DNS zones to associate with the private endpoint. If not set, no zone groups will be created and the private endpoint will not be associated with any private DNS zones. DNS records must be managed external to this module.
- `application_security_group_associations` - (Optional) A map of resource IDs of application security groups to associate with the private endpoint. The map key is deliberately arbitrary to avoid issues where map keys maybe unknown at plan time.
- `private_service_connection_name` - (Optional) The name of the private service connection. One will be generated if not set.
- `network_interface_name` - (Optional) The name of the network interface. One will be generated if not set.
- `location` - (Optional) The Azure location where the resources will be deployed. Defaults to the location of the resource group.
- `resource_group_name` - (Optional) The resource group resource ID where the private endpoint resources will be deployed. Defaults to the resource group of the parent resource.
- `ip_configurations` - (Optional) A map of IP configurations to create on the private endpoint. If not specified the platform will create one. The map key is deliberately arbitrary to avoid issues where map keys maybe unknown at plan time.
  - `name` - The name of the IP configuration.
  - `private_ip_address` - The private IP address of the IP configuration.
  - `member_name` - (Optional) The private IP configuration member name.

Type:

```hcl
map(object({
    name = optional(string, null)
    role_assignments = optional(map(object({
      name                                   = optional(string, null)
      role_definition_id_or_name             = string
      principal_id                           = string
      description                            = optional(string, null)
      skip_service_principal_aad_check       = optional(bool, false)
      condition                              = optional(string, null)
      condition_version                      = optional(string, null)
      delegated_managed_identity_resource_id = optional(string, null)
      principal_type                         = optional(string, null)
    })), {})
    lock = optional(object({
      kind  = string
      name  = optional(string, null)
      notes = optional(string, null)
    }), null)
    tags                                    = optional(map(string), null)
    subnet_resource_id                      = string
    subresource_name                        = optional(string, null) # only required if the parent resource exposes more than one private endpoint sub-resource
    private_dns_zone_group_name             = optional(string, "default")
    private_dns_zone_resource_ids           = optional(set(string), [])
    application_security_group_associations = optional(map(string), {})
    private_service_connection_name         = optional(string, null)
    network_interface_name                  = optional(string, null)
    location                                = optional(string, null)
    resource_group_name                     = optional(string, null)
    ip_configurations = optional(map(object({
      name               = string
      private_ip_address = string
      member_name        = optional(string)
    })), {})
  }))
```

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_private_endpoints_manage_dns_zone_group"></a> [private\_endpoints\_manage\_dns\_zone\_group](#input\_private\_endpoints\_manage\_dns\_zone\_group)

Description: Whether to manage private DNS zone groups with this module. If set to false, you must manage private DNS zone groups externally, e.g. using Azure Policy.

Type: `bool`

Default: `true`

### <a name="input_public_network_access_enabled"></a> [public\_network\_access\_enabled](#input\_public\_network\_access\_enabled)

Description: Allow access to the Grafana endpoint over the public network. The default, `null`, disables public access when
`private_endpoints` is not empty and enables it otherwise, so a workspace without private endpoints stays reachable.  
Set `true` or `false` to choose explicitly. The built-in Azure Policy "Azure Managed Grafana workspaces should disable  
public network access" audits, denies or modifies this setting: match it to avoid conflicts.

Type: `bool`

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_resource_types"></a> [resource\_types](#input\_resource\_types)

Description: Override the AzAPI `<provider>/<resource>@<api-version>` strings used by this module and its submodules. Each key defaults to a tested value; supply only the keys you want to override. Useful when targeting a sovereign cloud with older API versions, or when opting into a newer preview API.

- `authorization_locks` - Management locks applied to the workspace and its private endpoints.
- `authorization_role_assignments` - Role assignments on the workspace, on its private endpoints, and for its managed identity.
- `dashboard_grafana` - The Azure Managed Grafana workspace managed by this module.
- `insights_diagnostic_settings` - Diagnostic settings on the workspace.
- `network_private_endpoints` - Private endpoints to the workspace.
- `network_private_endpoints_private_dns_zone_groups` - Private DNS zone groups of the private endpoints.
- `dashboard_grafana_managed_private_endpoints` - Override slot for the `managed-private-endpoint` submodule. Defaults live in the submodule; supply only the keys you want to override.
  - `dashboard_grafana_managed_private_endpoints` - The managed private endpoint managed by the submodule.

Type:

```hcl
object({
    authorization_locks                               = optional(string, "Microsoft.Authorization/locks@2020-05-01")
    authorization_role_assignments                    = optional(string, "Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments@2022-04-01")
    dashboard_grafana                                 = optional(string, "Microsoft.Dashboard/grafana@2025-08-01")
    insights_diagnostic_settings                      = optional(string, "Microsoft.Insights/diagnosticSettings@2021-05-01-preview")
    network_private_endpoints                         = optional(string, "Microsoft.Network/privateEndpoints@2024-05-01")
    network_private_endpoints_private_dns_zone_groups = optional(string, "Microsoft.Network/privateEndpoints/privateDnsZoneGroups@2024-05-01")

    dashboard_grafana_managed_private_endpoints = optional(object({
      dashboard_grafana_managed_private_endpoints = optional(string)
    }), {})
  })
```

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_retry"></a> [retry](#input\_retry)

Description: Retry configuration applied to every `azapi` resource managed by the module (root resource and all submodules). Defaults to `null` (no custom retry).

- `error_message_regex`  - (Optional) A list of regex patterns matching error messages that trigger a retry.
- `interval_seconds`     - (Optional) Initial interval between retries in seconds.
- `max_interval_seconds` - (Optional) Maximum interval between retries in seconds.

See <https://registry.terraform.io/providers/Azure/azapi/latest/docs/resources/resource#retry> for full semantics.

Type:

```hcl
object({
    error_message_regex  = optional(list(string))
    interval_seconds     = optional(number)
    max_interval_seconds = optional(number)
  })
```

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_role_assignments"></a> [role\_assignments](#input\_role\_assignments)

Description: A map of role assignments to create on the Grafana workspace. The map key is deliberately arbitrary to avoid issues where map keys maybe unknown at plan time.

- `name` - (Optional) The name of the role assignment. If not set, a random UUID will be generated. Changing this forces the creation of a new resource.
- `role_definition_id_or_name` - The ID or name of the role definition to assign to the principal.
- `principal_id` - The ID of the principal to assign the role to.
- `description` - (Optional) The description of the role assignment.
- `skip_service_principal_aad_check` - (Optional) If set to true, skips the Azure Active Directory check for the service principal in the tenant. Defaults to false.
- `condition` - (Optional) The condition which will be used to scope the role assignment.
- `condition_version` - (Optional) The version of the condition syntax. Leave as `null` if you are not using a condition, if you are then valid values are '2.0'.
- `delegated_managed_identity_resource_id` - (Optional) The delegated Azure Resource Id which contains a Managed Identity. Changing this forces a new resource to be created. This field is only used in cross-tenant scenario.
- `principal_type` - (Optional) The type of the `principal_id`. Possible values are `User`, `Group` and `ServicePrincipal`. It is necessary to explicitly set this attribute when creating role assignments if the principal creating the assignment is constrained by ABAC rules that filters on the PrincipalType attribute.

> Note: only set `skip_service_principal_aad_check` to true if you are assigning a role to a service principal.

Type:

```hcl
map(object({
    name                                   = optional(string, null)
    role_definition_id_or_name             = string
    principal_id                           = string
    description                            = optional(string, null)
    skip_service_principal_aad_check       = optional(bool, false)
    condition                              = optional(string, null)
    condition_version                      = optional(string, null)
    delegated_managed_identity_resource_id = optional(string, null)
    principal_type                         = optional(string, null)
  }))
```

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_sku"></a> [sku](#input\_sku)

Description: The SKU of the Grafana workspace. Only `Standard` can be created; the `Essential` tier is deprecated and retires on 31 March 2027.

Type: `string`

Default: `"Standard"`

### <a name="input_sku_size"></a> [sku\_size](#input\_sku\_size)

Description: The instance size of the Standard tier: `X1` (500 alert rules) or `X2` (more memory, 1,000 alert rules). Size can be increased but not decreased. Defaults to `X1`.

Type: `string`

Default: `"X1"`

### <a name="input_smtp_password"></a> [smtp\_password](#input\_smtp\_password)

Description: The SMTP password, required whenever `grafana_configurations.smtp.user` is set. Write-only: never stored in plan or state. Supply it on every apply: Azure rejects workspace updates whose SMTP settings lack it.

Type: `string`

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_smtp_password_version"></a> [smtp\_password\_version](#input\_smtp\_password\_version)

Description: Change this value to push a rotated SMTP password without any other change. Only used when `grafana_configurations.smtp.user` is set.

Type: `string`

Default: `"1"`

### <a name="input_tags"></a> [tags](#input\_tags)

Description: (Optional) Tags of the resource.

Type: `map(string)`

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_timeouts"></a> [timeouts](#input\_timeouts)

Description: Default per-operation timeouts applied to every `azapi` resource managed by the module. Defaults to `null` (provider defaults). Each value is a Go duration string (e.g. `30m`, `1h`).

- `create` - (Optional) Timeout for create operations.
- `read`   - (Optional) Timeout for read operations.
- `update` - (Optional) Timeout for update operations.
- `delete` - (Optional) Timeout for delete operations.

Type:

```hcl
object({
    create = optional(string)
    read   = optional(string)
    update = optional(string)
    delete = optional(string)
  })
```

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_zone_redundancy_enabled"></a> [zone\_redundancy\_enabled](#input\_zone\_redundancy\_enabled)

Description: Enable zone redundancy. Recommended for production in the regions that support it (see "Reliability in Azure Managed  
Grafana" on Microsoft Learn); elsewhere the deployment fails. Incurs an additional cost. It can only be chosen when the  
workspace is created: changing it replaces the workspace and everything stored in it. Defaults to `false`, so that the  
module deploys in every region.

Type: `bool`

Default: `false`

## Outputs

The following outputs are exported:

### <a name="output_endpoint"></a> [endpoint](#output\_endpoint)

Description: The URL of the Grafana workspace, e.g. `https://<name>-<hash>.<region>.grafana.azure.com`.

### <a name="output_grafana_version"></a> [grafana\_version](#output\_grafana\_version)

Description: The full Grafana version currently running on the workspace.

### <a name="output_managed_private_endpoints"></a> [managed\_private\_endpoints](#output\_managed\_private\_endpoints)

Description: A map of the managed private endpoints created, keyed like `var.managed_private_endpoints`, with their resource ID and connection status.

### <a name="output_name"></a> [name](#output\_name)

Description: The name of the Grafana workspace.

### <a name="output_outbound_ips"></a> [outbound\_ips](#output\_outbound\_ips)

Description: The outbound IPs of the workspace when `deterministic_outbound_ip_enabled` is `true`.

### <a name="output_private_endpoints"></a> [private\_endpoints](#output\_private\_endpoints)

Description: A map of the private endpoints created, keyed like `var.private_endpoints`, with their resource ID and network interface IDs.

### <a name="output_resource_id"></a> [resource\_id](#output\_resource\_id)

Description: The resource ID of the Grafana workspace.

### <a name="output_system_assigned_mi_principal_id"></a> [system\_assigned\_mi\_principal\_id](#output\_system\_assigned\_mi\_principal\_id)

Description: The principal ID of the system-assigned managed identity, or `null` when it is not enabled.
